note: Two uncommitted experiments on the inline-topic parent, measured and reverted. Uniform plain batches (one key size, one value size, one-byte timestamp delta, no headers, one- or two-byte offset deltas) were decoded from fixed markers instead of per-field varints. A unit test crossed the 64-record offset-delta width change and matched the generic decoder. Eight interleaved pairs: before median 626,790.01, after median 609,768.02, paired mean ratio 0.986, bootstrap 95% CI 0.911 to 1.067, four of eight slower. Client CPU-nanoseconds per record mean ratio 1.024. Decoding the same batches on one thread per partition, only when the framed response already fit in buffer_memory, was slower: paired mean ratio 0.933, CI 0.879 to 0.989, six of eight slower, CPU mean ratio 1.210. Both were reverted. This is not a peer comparison and not a fastest-client result.
